subject: Key Transit Agreement & Network Attachment Plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: security@acmehealth.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed Key Transit Agreement + Network Attachment Plan

Hi Alice / Acme security team,

Following our kickoff, attached is a concise proposal for the Key Transit Agreement and the network attachment topology we discussed. High-level asks: an agreed CIDR for the peer, allowed management IPs, and the PoP evidence types Acme needs for BYOK and HSM custody.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Transport: mTLS over private peering (IPsec optional) between your VPC and our dedicated VPC. We prefer mutual TLS to keep packet inspection simple for your compliance team.
- BYOK flow: Customer KEK-wrap at rest before upload. Redwood will accept wrapped keys and import to an HSM-backed KMS inside the private deployment. Keys are marked customer-owned; Redwood operator cannot export raw key material.
- Rotation: recommended 90-day KEK rotation cadence; emergency rewrap within 24 hours for compromise scenarios.
- Audit: full KMS audit logs (immutable), HSM attestation report at cutover, and operator separation evidence.

Open questions for Acme (please confirm):
1) Preferred peering model: IPsec VPN or AWS Transit Gateway direct attachment?
2) Which external IP range will you use for eBGP/static? (we need 2 /30s if using BGP)
3) POA for evidence: SOC2 Type II + HSM vendor attestation sufficient, or do you need additional FHIR-specific controls?

Attachments included: rdwd-key-transit-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal), acme-network-attachment-draft.svg (diagram).

Next steps: if the approach looks good I propose a 45-minute working session this week to lock the CIDRs and cutover window.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Naomi — thanks for the proposal, looks good on first pass. A few clarifying points from Acme security: 

- We prefer IPsec VPN for initial cutover (we can revisit TGW direct attach later once legal clears the contract).
- For BYOK: we need clarity on the unwrap boundary. Will Redwood ever perform an unwrap outside of an HSM? We require a written guarantee that unwrapped key material never leaves the HSM in any environment.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 Type II + HSM vendor attestation is baseline. For production PHI workloads we also require a signed PoP (proof of possession) for initial key import and a periodic attestation (quarterly) that keys remain under customer control.

Can we get that detail documented in an appendix? Also request: can Redwood provide the expected public IPs for the VPN endpoints and a pcap retention policy for <48 hours?

Thanks — happy to lock a time on Wed 9:00am ET for the working session if that works.

Alice Park

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Thanks Alice — good questions. Below are concrete answers we can include in the appendix for the agreement. I also attached a short custody checklist for Acme's procurement/security review.

On unwrap boundary and operator guarantees
- Redwood will never perform key unwrapping outside an HSM. The import path is: customer wraps CEK with customer KEK locally -> uploads the wrapped material to Redwood -> wrapped CEK is stored encrypted at rest -> HSM in the customer's private VPC performs unwrap only inside HSM firmware and creates an HSM-backed key handle; raw key bytes are never exported. We will include this as a contractual guarantee in Appendix A ("Unwrap Boundary & Operator Controls").

Rotation cadence & emergency rewrap
- Standard cadence: KEK rotation every 90 days (customer-triggered).
- Emergency: we define an "Incident Rewrap SLA" of 24 hours from agreement to target rewrap completion; the plan includes pre-authorized runbooks and a dry-run checklist.

Network & peering
- For IPsec: we'll provide two candidate public IPs for the Redwood endpoint as soon as legal signs the MSA. We will permit an allowlist of up to 8 management IPs for operator access (mutual TLS + Identity-based egress).
- PCAP/telemetry: Redwood retains minimal PCAP for troubleshooting for up to 36 hours by default and redacts payloads. If Acme needs <48 hours retention we can set that as the default in the attachment.

Audit & attestation
- At cutover we provide: HSM vendor attestation, immutable KMS audit export (signed snapshot), and a signed PoP for initial key import. Quarterly attestation can be delivered as a signed statement by Redwood's security team.

Attached: kms-custody-checklist.xlsx (checklist for procurement)

If this looks good I will schedule the Wed working session (Wed 2026-06-09 09:00 ET) and loop in legal for the Appendix wording.

Best,
Jordan Blake
